selectedCourseEvidence.description2: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. selectedCourseEvidence.description2:
Public health is about changing the world. From pandemics to lifestyle-related diseases, from screening for disease to improving water and air quality, it asks: how can we improve to keep the population healthy?_x000D_
But how do we know what actually works? In this course you will dive into epidemiology: the science behind public health. You will learn how to study disease, risks, and changes over time, and how to critically evaluate evidence. Because behind every public health decision lies a question of evidence, and by the end of this course, you will be equipped to engage with it. This course invites you to look beyond the lab, the hospital, and the library, into the wider world where health is shaped. What matters most if we truly care about health, and how can we influence that?
selectedCourseEvidence.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
selectedCourseEvidence.profile: Introduces epidemiological reasoning and its application to public health. Students measure and interpret disease patterns, study research designs, association, bias, confounding and causality, then examine health determinants, promotion, needs assessment and screening. A local project analyzes a Zeeland health challenge, compares population data, considers affected groups and interventions, and incorporates stakeholder perspectives into feasible recommendations.

selectedCourseEvidence.methods: Epidemiological rate and risk calculation; Descriptive and analytic epidemiology; Study-design and evidence appraisal; Population-health data interpretation; Outbreak analysis; Health-needs assessment; Stakeholder interviewing; Evidence-informed intervention development

selectedCourseEvidence.description2: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? selectedCourseEvidence.description2: Explores human development across the lifespan. Examines physical, cognitive, emotional and social changes from prenatal life to old age and develops critical thinking about factors influencing individual uniqueness.
selectedCourseEvidence.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
selectedCourseEvidence.profile: Examines physical, cognitive, emotional, social and personality development from prenatal life through old age and death. Biological and environmental influences are considered alongside attachment, education, relationships, cultural differences and developmental psychopathology. Students connect theoretical perspectives to case studies, assessment and interventions at different life stages. A life-story interview with an adult over fifty applies developmental concepts through interviewing, analysis and a written report.
selectedCourseEvidence.topics: Developmental theories; Genetics and environment; Prenatal development and birth; Infancy and attachment; Cognitive and psychomotor development; Early and middle childhood; Play and education; Adolescence and psychopathology; Emerging and early adulthood; Middle and late adulthood; Relationships and personality development; Care and developmental interventions; Death, dying, grief and bereavement
selectedCourseEvidence.methods: Life-story interviewing; Theory-guided lifespan interview analysis; Developmental case-study analysis; Critical appraisal of developmental research and assessment reports

conceptAssessment: Three substantial AI-method backbones respond to this interdisciplinary target: hybrid cognition/experimental behaviour, technical computer systems, and health/behaviour domain foundations. Programming, inference, logic, optimisation, reinforcement learning, ML/neural/vision/robotics and mathematical preparation are substantive. Biological/social/health courses provide the stated specific domain knowledge; no clinical AI system, social robot or full computational behaviour implementation is guaranteed. Description-only ReinforcementLearning, Psycholinguistics, PerceptionAction, AdvancedCalculus and NetworksDatabase courses receive full actual-content consideration without inferred detailed methods.

schedules.label: Hybrid intelligence and human cognition
schedules.concept: Combines programming, machine learning, logic and agent decision making with cognitive science, perception and human behaviour. Ethics and experimental behavioural methods frame how intelligent systems interact with people; this is a broad AI programme rather than a replica of the VU thesis and project sequence. General or biological courses supply their stated foundations; no specialised human–robot interaction, clinical AI, computational language project or independent AI thesis is guaranteed.
schedules.labelReason: The completed curriculum includes extensive technical AI as well as cognition, interaction and ethics; hybrid intelligence describes the actual combination.
progression: Current offerings and formal prerequisites checked for all placements. Programming and calculus precede required advanced courses; at least six 300-level courses, four per term, 24 unique selections and Year-1 PPD. Retained foundation-before-advanced sequencing where feasible; no invented formal prerequisites. Machine Learning has no formal prerequisite; its mathematical preparation remains advisory.
traceOverrides: develops experimental-design and multivariable statistical evaluation of behavioural evidence, supporting human-centred model assessment without promising an AI project

candidateStopping.assessment: Three conceptually distinct, evidenced UCR curricula pass the 24-course and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates: broad hybrid intelligence and cognition, technical AI system construction, and health/behaviour applications. The energy-systems interest is a separate application direction but the approved maximum of three alternatives is already reached; the isolated teaching direction lacks a specific UCR teacher-education sequence. Re-audit retains three qualified responses only because each has a substantial actual AI-method backbone and a distinct subject emphasis. Domain health/behaviour courses are not claimed to implement specialist medical AI. Sustainable-energy AI remains an unselected direction at the maximum of three, not a claim that generic AI courses alone provide energy engineering.
